entities.summary:
Cao Hong (b. 169 CE, China) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in China.

As a military leader and commander, Cao Hong played a crucial role in maintaining stability and order in the region during a time of great turmoil.

His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of Chinese administration and governance for centuries to come.

The Cao Wei dynasty, which Cao Hong served, was a major force in Chinese history, leaving a lasting impact on the country's politics, culture, and society.

"The art of war is of vital importance to the State;

it is a matter of life and death, a road either to safety or to ruin.

He who knows it will always be victorious; those who do not will always be defeated." - Sun Tzu, The Art of War
